The Senior Lead, Training, based at New Delhi (India Country Office) will be part of the team supporting the Jharkhand Foundational Literacy Program and lead the planning, implementation and monitoring of its orientation and capacity-building programs. The role will oversee training delivery for approximately 200–300 team members annually, including block-level staff, Team Leads and District Leads. Using assessment results, facilitator observations and field feedback, the Senior Lead, Training will identify learning gaps, coordinate corrective sessions and refreshers, and strengthen the approach for subsequent cohorts.

Responsibilities:

Define role-specific training needs and learning outcomes:

Develop a strong understanding of the Jharkhand Foundational Literacy Program, including implementation model, staffing structure and expected outcomes, and translate this into role‑wise learning needs.
Define role‑wise capabilities and learning outcomes for each participant group and training component, in consultation with Program, technical and other relevant teams.
Specify assessment criteria and deployment gates (mandatory modules and minimum competency thresholds) for independent field work.

Agency onboarding & management:

Serve as the primary Room to Read point of contact for the external training agency and anchor day-to-day coordination throughout the assignment.
 Lead the agency onboarding by facilitating access to relevant program information, internal stakeholders, existing training materials, policies and other required resources.
Monitor agency progress against the agreed workplan and follow up on pending activities, submissions and actions and coordinate internal review and approval of agency deliverables.

Internal stakeholder & content coordination:

Coordinate across departments involved in the orientation and capacity-building programme.
Coordinate review meetings, consultations, content validation, facilitator discussions and approvals required at different stages.
Ensure that inputs received from multiple teams are consolidated and communicated clearly to the agency.
Coordinate with relevant Room to Read staff who are expected to facilitate or contribute to specific training sessions.

Lead training planning and implementation for 250+ staff across different roles and phases:

Lead Room to Read’s end‑to‑end training plan for approximately 250+ staff across different roles and phases, aligned to hiring phases, district calendars and deployment targets.
Sequence agency‑led sessions, Room to Read‑led technical sessions, field‑based learning and refresher interventions so that all required components are delivered in the right order and on schedule.
Support preparation and execution of the second training phase by incorporating learning and operational experience from the first cohort and refresher cycle.
Resolve implementation issues during training and ensure smooth coordination across batches and locations.
Lead planning and coordination of training logistics for each batch, including venues, participant travel and accommodation, equipment and materials,

in coordination with Admin, Finance and other teams.

Training monitoring, quality & learning follow-up:

Maintain and review a training dashboard covering planned and completed batches, attendance, completion, assessments, feedback, learning progress and pending actions, disaggregated by cohort and role..
Analyse participant assessment results, feedback, facilitator observations and agency reports to identify recurring learning gaps and implementation issues, and plan corrective actions.
Plan and coordinate refresher trainings based on identified needs, and agree additional support (repeat sessions, practice, coaching or reassessment) for participants who have not demonstrated required competencies.

Room to Read offers a competitive salary with excellent benefits. Benefits include thirteenth month bonus, health insurance and a retirement plan. The non-monetary compensation includes a unique opportunity to be part of an innovative, meaningful, and rapidly growing organization which is transforming the lives of millions of children in developing countries on literacy and gender equality in education.

Room to Read is a child-safe organization

Read is a child-safe organization; all personnel must adhere to Room to Read’s Child Protection Policy, Child Protection Code of Conduct and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) Policy.

Room to Read is an equal opportunity employer committed to identifying and developing the skills and leadership of people from diverse backgrounds.

Child Protection Principles
Room to Read is committed to the education and welfare of children and protecting them from abuse and exploitation
Room to Read has zero tolerance for child abuse and exploitation.
All children have the right to be free from abuse and exploitation, including neglect, maltreatment, and physical, mental or sexual violence, injury or abuse.
All children should be treated with respect and dignity.
The well-being of the child is Room to Read’s first priority when dealing with all identified or suspected cases of child abuse.
Room to Read shall integrate child protection into all its organizational strategies, structures and work practices.

Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) Principles
Room to Read Representatives must create and maintain an environment that prevents sexual exploitation and sexual abuse.
Room to Read has zero tolerance for adult sexual exploitation and abuse.
Sexual exploitation and abuse are serious violations of fundamental human rights and will not be accepted or tolerated.
All adults should be treated with respect and dignity.
Room to Read implements a survivor-centered approach, putting the survivor’s rights and dignity at the forefront.
Survivors referred to available professional assistance (e.g. mental health counselling), upon consent.

About Room to Read:

Founded in 2000 on the belief that World Change Starts with Educated Children®, Room to Read envisions a world free from illiteracy and gender inequality, where all children have room to read, learn and grow – creating lasting change. Through our Literacy Portfolio, we train and coach teachers of the early grades in literacy instruction; create and publish quality books and curricular materials in local languages; and establish children’s libraries filled with diverse children’s books that can be enjoyed at school and home. Our Gender Equality Portfolio supports adolescents, particularly girls, in developing life skills that promote gender equality, helping them to pursue lifelong learning and make informed decisions.

We support young people of all genders to overcome gender biases and build the knowledge and skills to create a gender-equal world. Room to Read collaborates with local communities, partner organizations, publishers, and governments to test and implement innovative models that can be integrated into the education system to deliver positive outcomes for children at scale. To date, Room to Read has benefited more than 50 million children in 28 countries.

Job Description

Position Teacher

Reports to School Coordinator

Door Step School (DSS) was established in Mumbai, India in 1989 with the aim of addressing

literacy amongst the marginalized sections of society. The school provides education and

support to the often-forgotten children of pavement dwellers, slum dwellers and construction

site families. The school has since expanded to cover both Mumbai and Pune and has

reached over 25,000 children since inception. Many of these children are not enrolled in

school and have limited access to books and a place to study. Additionally, many children

(particularly girls) drop out of school to work or care for younger children . With neither

support nor resources at home some children also suffer from very low learning levels.

Door Step School is an NGO that has worked for the last 20 years to bring literacy and

education to children of various marginalized communities in Mumbai and Pune. To address

various associated issues, Door Step School runs a network of on-site centers with pre-

school (balwadi) programs; study centers with dedicated teachers to provide tuition support;

community/reference libraries to provide a broad array of study materials and non formal

education classes for working children remain children out of school. These programs are the

four pillars that deal with the problem of non enrollment, stagnation and wastage. Door Step

School has also expanded its activities to include computer classes in some of its locations.

DSS teachers will create close relationships with students and their families to provide the

students with a high caliber education that enables them to easily transition to formal schools.

Teachers will be responsible for recognizing gaps in a child’s education and developing and

implementing curriculum to develop a child’s intellectual and social skills.

Key Areas of Responsibilities:

1. Assist team leader/coordinator in developing community relations and encouraging

families to enroll their children in school.

2. Create and maintain an inviting learning environment.

3. Create lesson plans that engage students and develop their intellectual and social

skills.

4. Administrative responsibilities.

Specific Responsibilities:

1. Assist Team Leader/Coordinator in developing community relations and

encouraging families to enroll their children in school

 Assist team leader / coordinator with conducting a door to door community survey

 Identify new children to enroll

 Build rapport with parents through home visits and parents meetings

 Following up on irregular children in the class, ensuring high percentage of attendance

in class

 Collect community contributions.

Door Step School

2. Create and maintain an inviting learning environment

 Make optimum use of the classroom space

 Ensure that materials needed for class are requisitioned and received on time

 Ensure class is clean and materials needed for the day are prepared before class

begins

 Record attendance daily and employ methods by which to encourage high levels of

attendance

 Build a rapport with and amongst the children and create an environment where

children are encouraged to learn, share and express themselves

 Use democratic techniques of disciplining

 Write monthly reports that includes statistical data on student attendance and

performance, information on special events, interesting observations of children, case

studies and success stories

3. Create lesson plans that engage students and develop their intellectual and social

skills

 Use a variety of methods to ensure cooperative, effective and active learning that

builds rational, reflective and analytical thinking

 Develop curriculum and activities that:

-Builds vocabulary and develop language skills

-Builds social skills

-Encourages questioning and critical thinking

-Encourages student participation in the class

-Encourages observation of the physical and social environment

-Builds confidence and self esteem of the student

 Prepare tests and question papers to accurately measure student progress

 Conduct parent meetings wherein information on a student’s academic and non-

academic performance is shared

 Conduct ongoing assessments of the students and tailor curriculum to fill gaps when

needed

5. Administrative Responsibilities

 Conduct basic accounting duties for community contributions, petty cash, conveyance

reimbursements

 Keep stock registers

Required Competencies

 Able to use limited resources optimally

 Willing to employ a variety of teaching methods that make learning active, fun and

effective

 Able to accurately gauge areas in which students need improvement and develop

lessons to meet those needs including assigning work appropriately

 Comfortable working with diverse students who often come from difficult backgrounds

 Able to serve as a role model for children in the class

Pay: From ₹12,000.00 per month

Preschool Teacher / Early Years Educator

Position: Preschool Teacher / Early Years Educator

Department: Academic / Early Years

Reporting To: Centre Head / Head of School

Location: Maple Bear Canadian Preschool, Sector 71, Gurugram

Key Responsibilities

1. Child Development & Learning Outcomes

\* Plan and implement age-appropriate learning experiences aligned with the Maple Bear curriculum, learning objectives, and developmental outcomes.

\* Prepare lesson plans that integrate cognitive, language, social, emotional, physical, and motor development.

\* Observe and understand individual children’s developmental needs, interests, strengths, and areas requiring support.

\* Track developmental milestones and maintain appropriate observations and records for each child.

\* Provide individualised support and adapt activities wherever required to meet varied learning needs.

\* Create opportunities for children to develop independence, confidence, communication, creativity, and problem-solving skills.

2. Classroom Instruction & Activity Planning

\* Design and conduct engaging, hands-on, play-based, and experiential learning activities.

\* Use storytelling, music, art, craft, role-play, sensory activities, movement, outdoor play, and other age-appropriate methods.

\* Ensure effective implementation of the daily schedule and classroom routines.

\* Make learning interactive, child-centred, and developmentally appropriate.

\* Use classroom resources and learning materials effectively and responsibly.

\* Ensure activities are planned in advance and all required materials are ready before the class begins.

\* Encourage children to explore, ask questions, experiment, and learn through experience.

3. Classroom Environment & Presentation

\* Maintain a clean, organised, attractive, and stimulating classroom environment.

\* Ensure the classroom is presentable and aligned with the standards and requirements communicated by the Academic and Business teams.

\* Display children’s work, learning resources, themes, and classroom materials appropriately.

\* Ensure learning corners, activity areas, displays, and classroom resources are updated regularly.

\* Take responsibility for the proper upkeep and use of classroom resources and materials.

4. Child Safety, Health & Well-being

\* Ensure a safe, hygienic, caring, and emotionally supportive classroom environment.

\* Closely monitor children during classroom activities, transitions, outdoor play, meals, nap time, and other routines.

\* Follow all school safety, child protection, hygiene, and emergency protocols.

\* Never leave children unattended.

\* Identify and promptly report any injury, illness, unusual behaviour, or safety concern to the Centre Head/management.

\* Maintain appropriate hygiene practices and encourage children to develop healthy habits.

\* Support children’s emotional well-being and provide reassurance, comfort, and age-appropriate guidance.

5. Behaviour Management & Social-Emotional Development

\* Promote positive behaviour through encouragement, modelling, and positive reinforcement.

\* Teach children sharing, cooperation, empathy, respect, patience, and appropriate communication.

\* Handle classroom behaviour and conflicts calmly and constructively.

\* Support children in developing emotional regulation and problem-solving skills.

\* Follow the school’s approach to positive discipline and avoid inappropriate disciplinary practices.

\* Maintain a positive and inclusive classroom environment where every child feels valued and supported.

6. Parent Communication & Engagement

\* Maintain professional and respectful communication with parents regarding children’s learning, development, behaviour, and day-to-day experiences.

\* Share relevant observations and updates with parents through approved school communication channels.

\* Participate actively in Parent-Teacher Meetings, parent workshops, orientations, events, and other parent engagement activities.

\* Address parent queries professionally and escalate concerns to the Centre Head whenever required.

\* Maintain confidentiality regarding children, families, staff, and school matters.

\* Work collaboratively with parents to support children’s learning and development at home and at school.

7. Documentation, Assessment & Reporting

\* Maintain accurate attendance records and other classroom documentation.

\* Prepare lesson plans and maintain assessment and observation records as per school requirements.

\* Maintain individual child portfolios and developmental documentation.

\* Record and report children’s progress, observations, achievements, and areas requiring support.

\* Complete assessments and reports within the stipulated timelines.

\* Document and immediately report any incidents, accidents, injuries, or safeguarding concerns as per school protocol.

\* Ensure all academic and administrative records are accurate and up to date.

8. Daily Team Coordination & School Operations

\* Participate in regular daily team meetings to align on upcoming activities, events, PTMs, classroom requirements, and other operational matters.

\* Coordinate with fellow teachers and support staff for smooth functioning of the centre.

\* Support school events, celebrations, workshops, field trips, special activities, and other centre initiatives.

\* Ensure timely preparation for events and classroom activities.

\* Follow the school calendar, academic calendar, daily schedule, and operational processes.

\* Support daycare activities or other assigned responsibilities when required.

\* Maintain punctuality, attendance, professional conduct, and adherence to school policies.

9. Collaboration with Academic & Central Teams

\* Work closely with the Centre Head, Academic Team, Business Team, and Central Team to ensure consistent implementation of school standards.

\* Participate in teacher training, curriculum training, certification programmes, workshops, and professional development initiatives.

\* Implement feedback received through classroom observations and academic reviews.

\* Continuously develop knowledge of early childhood education, child development, classroom practices, and emerging educational approaches.

10. Marketing & Digital Support

\* Coordinate with the Digital/Marketing Team for school-related online promotions and communication requirements.

\* Share good-quality photographs, videos, classroom activities, celebrations, and learning moments as required, while strictly following school guidelines regarding children’s privacy and consent.

\* Support the creation of content showcasing classroom learning and school activities.

\* Provide inputs and creative requirements to the relevant team in advance for events, activities, and promotional initiatives.

\* Maintain professional representation of the school across all communication and promotional activities.

11. Professional Development

\* Participate actively in all mandatory training, workshops, meetings, and professional development programmes.

\* Complete required teacher training and certifications in alignment with the Maple Bear Central/Academic Team.

\* Stay updated on best practices in early childhood education, child development, play-based learning, and experiential education.

\* Seek continuous improvement based on feedback, observations, and professional learning.

⸻

Key Performance Areas

The teacher will be evaluated on:

\* Effective implementation of the Maple Bear curriculum.

\* Quality and preparedness of lesson plans and classroom activities.

\* Children’s engagement and learning outcomes.

\* Individual child observation and developmental tracking.

\* Classroom management and environment.

\* Child safety, hygiene, and well-being.

\* Parent communication and relationship management.

\* Accuracy and timely completion of documentation.

\* Participation in meetings, events, training, and school initiatives.

\* Teamwork, professionalism, punctuality, and adherence to school policies.

\* Contribution to the overall academic and operational standards of the centre.

Qualifications & Experience

\* Graduate degree in any relevant discipline; NTT/ECCE/Montessori/ECE qualification preferred.

\* Prior experience in preschool/early years education preferred.

\* Good communication and interpersonal skills.

\* Strong understanding of early childhood development and play-based learning.

\* Ability to work collaboratively as part of a team.

\* Passion for working with young children.

\* Positive, patient, caring, and child-centric approach.

Core Competencies

\* Planning & organisation

\* Creativity and activity design

\* Observation and documentation

\* Team collaboration

\* Emotional intelligence

\* Professionalism and accountability

\* Adaptability and willingness to learn

We Grow Teachers into Leaders.

We're Building Our Founding Team!

At Dreamtime Early Years, we believe that when you invest in teachers, nurture their potential, and encourage continuous learning, extraordinary things happen.

Our vision goes beyond providing quality early childhood education. We want to create an environment where educators discover their strengths, develop their skills, take on new responsibilities, and grow into future leaders in education.

Our experience has shown us that teachers can go on to lead teams, shape curriculum, and contribute to teacher development and school leadership. At Dreamtime Early Years, your professional growth matters as much as the growth of every child in your care.

Come for the opportunity to teach. Stay for the opportunity to grow. Rise to become the leader you never imagined you could be.

We are looking for passionate, caring, curious, and committed educators to join our founding team.

Position 1: Lead Preschool Teacher

Role Overview

As a Lead Preschool Teacher, you will play a key role in creating a joyful, engaging, and developmentally appropriate learning environment for young children. You will lead classroom activities, plan meaningful learning experiences, and work closely with parents and colleagues to support each child's overall development.

This is an opportunity to build your teaching expertise, contribute to the school's early-years learning culture, and develop the leadership skills to grow into future academic and school leadership roles.

Plan and deliver age-appropriate, play-based learning experiences that support children's cognitive, social, emotional, physical, and language development.

Observe children's development, document their progress, and identify individual learning needs.

Build meaningful relationships with parents and communicate children's progress effectively.

Establish positive classroom routines and encourage independence, creativity, curiosity, and collaboration.

Collaborate with support teachers and the school leadership team to ensure high-quality classroom experiences.

Participate in teacher training, curriculum planning, reflective practice, and continuous professional development.

Contribute ideas, share best practices, and take initiative in improving teaching and learning.

Demonstrate the potential to mentor fellow educators and take on future leadership responsibilities.

Position 2: Preschool Support Teacher

Role Overview

As a Preschool Support Teacher, you will work closely with the Lead Preschool Teacher to create a caring, safe, and engaging learning environment. You will help children explore, learn, build confidence, and develop essential early-life skills.

At Dreamtime Early Years, this role is more than classroom assistance. It is an opportunity to strengthen your teaching abilities, understand early childhood education, and build a pathway towards becoming an independent teacher and future educational leader.

Assist the Lead Preschool Teacher in implementing lesson plans and daily classroom activities.

Support children during play-based learning, storytelling, art and craft, music, movement, and group activities.

_Job Description_

*Department: *Early Childhood / Kindergarten

*Training stage: *Year 1

*Working relationships: *Class Teacher and Coordinator

*Role purpose*

Support the Class Teacher in creating a warm, safe and nurturing Waldorf kindergarten environment. Assist with daily classroom rhythms, child care, creative activities and school programmes while developing teaching skills through observation, mentorship and Year 1 training.

*Classroom support*

Assist the Class Teacher with daily activities, sessions and transitions, including morning circle songs, verses and seasonal movement.

Support wet-on-wet watercolour painting, beeswax modelling, form drawing and seasonal crafts.

Prepare the seasonal and nature tables, art materials and snack setup before school. Keep the classroom tidy, warm and aesthetically aligned with Waldorf principles, and restore order after sessions.

Prepare props, the story corner and puppet setups as directed by the Coordinator.

*Child care and supervision*

Provide attentive, calm supervision during free play, snacks, transitions and outdoor activities. Respond patiently to children’s physical, emotional and social needs.

Build individual connections with every child and address children by name. Offer additional support to children who are shy, new or experiencing separation anxiety.

Allow children to lead their creative play, intervening when safety or wellbeing requires it.

Report wellbeing concerns promptly and confidentially to the Coordinator. Know and follow school emergency and first-aid protocols.

*Observation and Year 1 training*

Keep a regular observation journal covering classroom rhythms, activities, play patterns and personal reflections. Document children’s physical, social, emotional and creative development.

Attend weekly mentorship check-ins with the Class Teacher, prepared with observations and questions.

Attend Waldorf orientation, internal workshops and staff development days. Read recommended early childhood texts and submit a brief monthly reading reflection.

Develop personal artistic skills, including singing, knitting, sewing and beeswax work.

Swadhaa | Kindergarten Teacher |

*Classroom administration and materials*

Mark daily attendance accurately and flag unexplained absences to the Coordinator.

Update the materials inventory monthly and report replenishment needs for paints, beeswax, yarn, natural materials and snack supplies.

Care for classroom resources, including washing brushes, storing beeswax correctly and maintaining fabrics and natural items. Regularly source seasonal leaves, stones, flowers and pods for the nature table.

Assist with parent notices, newsletters and seasonal letters. Obtain the Coordinator’s review before dispatch.

Complete and submit a monthly classroom safety and hygiene checklist to the Coordinator.

*Festivals and school events*

Participate creatively in seasonal celebrations, including Diwali, Advent and Harvest. Help prepare decorations, costumes, food and festival setups.

Support parent evenings, open days, performances and outings. Complete assigned event logistics punctually and reliably.

*Parent interaction*

Greet parents warmly and professionally at drop-off and pick-up, maintaining appropriate communication boundaries.

Refer parent queries, concerns and discussions about children’s development to the Coordinator rather than addressing these independently.

Protect children’s personal information and family circumstances at all times.

*Professional conduct and safeguarding*

Arrive before children, maintain consistent attendance and follow school leave procedures.

Work respectfully with colleagues, staff and volunteers. Reflect Waldorf values in manner, speech and dress.

Avoid personal mobile devices or screens in the classroom or in view of children.

Maintain confidentiality about children, families, staff and school affairs. Do not share school matters on personal social media or with people outside the school community.

Report safeguarding concerns or ethical issues to the Coordinator. If not addressed, escalate immediately to the Academic Head.

*Role requirements and employment details*

This role calls for patience, warmth, careful observation, reliability, confidentiality, teamwork and a willingness to learn Waldorf early childhood practices. Required qualifications, prior experience, formal reporting line, location, working hours and employment type are to be confirmed by the school.

*1. Role Overview*

Responsible for the academic planning, teacher supervision, student development, parent coordination, safety, and day-to-day functioning of the Pre-Primary Section, ensuring age-appropriate learning and smooth school operations.

*2. Key Roles and Responsibilities*

*A. Academic Planning and Curriculum*

* Plan and monitor implementation of the approved Pre-Primary curriculum, ensuring timely completion of annual plans, monthly planners, weekly plans, and lesson plans.
* Monitor teaching quality through classroom observations, lesson-plan reviews, and feedback to teachers.
* Ensure age-appropriate, activity-based, and play-based learning to develop foundational literacy, numeracy, communication, creativity, and social skills.
* Monitor student progress and ensure appropriate developmental assessments, progress reports, and learning support plans.

*B. Teacher Management*

* Supervise teachers' classroom delivery, attendance, punctuality, lesson planning, and completion of assigned responsibilities.
* Conduct regular classroom observations and provide actionable feedback to improve teaching effectiveness.
* Plan teacher training, conduct academic meetings, and monitor faculty performance against assigned KRAs and KPIs.
* Manage teacher timetables, substitution arrangements, and classroom duty allocation.

*C. Student Safety and Development*

* Monitor students' academic, behavioural, social, emotional, and physical development.
* Ensure proper student supervision during classroom activities, breaks, outdoor play, arrival, and dispersal.
* Ensure compliance with child safeguarding, hygiene, authorised student handover, and emergency procedures.
* Address student behavioural concerns and coordinate additional support wherever required.

*D. Parent Coordination*

* Conduct parent-teacher meetings and communicate student progress, developmental concerns, and classroom-related updates.
* Address parent queries, document concerns, coordinate resolutions, and escalate sensitive matters to school leadership.

*E. School Operations and Events*

*F. Documentation and Reporting*

* Classroom observation and teacher mentoring.
* Student safety awareness, patience, empathy, and professional integrity.

*6. Accountability*

A reputed confidential partner school in Thane, Mumbai, is seeking an accomplished and dynamic *Head of School / Principal* to lead the institution's academic, administrative, operational, and strategic functions.

The ideal candidate must have substantial experience working in an *ICSE or IGCSE school environment*, along with a proven track record in school leadership, academic excellence, faculty development, parent engagement, admissions, and institutional growth.

The Principal will work closely with the CEO / Owner to implement the school's vision, strengthen academic outcomes, build a high-performing team, and ensure smooth and effective school operations.

*1. Strategic Leadership & School Development*

* Provide overall leadership and direction for the school.

* Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) across academics, admissions, operations, faculty, and student outcomes.
* Drive a culture of accountability, innovation, excellence, and continuous improvement.

* Oversee curriculum planning, implementation, assessment, and academic reporting.

IELTS Examiner and training status

Job Description

Position Teacher

Reports to School Coordinator

Door Step School (DSS) was established in Mumbai, India in 1989 with the aim of addressing

literacy amongst the marginalized sections of society. The school provides education and

support to the often-forgotten children of pavement dwellers, slum dwellers and construction

site families. The school has since expanded to cover both Mumbai and Pune and has

reached over 25,000 children since inception. Many of these children are not enrolled in

school and have limited access to books and a place to study. Additionally, many children

(particularly girls) drop out of school to work or care for younger children . With neither

support nor resources at home some children also suffer from very low learning levels.

Door Step School is an NGO that has worked for the last 20 years to bring literacy and

education to children of various marginalized communities in Mumbai and Pune. To address

various associated issues, Door Step School runs a network of on-site centers with pre-

school (balwadi) programs; study centers with dedicated teachers to provide tuition support;

community/reference libraries to provide a broad array of study materials and non formal

education classes for working children remain children out of school. These programs are the

four pillars that deal with the problem of non enrollment, stagnation and wastage. Door Step

School has also expanded its activities to include computer classes in some of its locations.

DSS teachers will create close relationships with students and their families to provide the

students with a high caliber education that enables them to easily transition to formal schools.

Teachers will be responsible for recognizing gaps in a child’s education and developing and

implementing curriculum to develop a child’s intellectual and social skills.

Key Areas of Responsibilities:

1. Assist team leader/coordinator in developing community relations and encouraging

families to enroll their children in school.

2. Create and maintain an inviting learning environment.

3. Create lesson plans that engage students and develop their intellectual and social

skills.

4. Administrative responsibilities.

Specific Responsibilities:

1. Assist Team Leader/Coordinator in developing community relations and

encouraging families to enroll their children in school

 Assist team leader / coordinator with conducting a door to door community survey

 Identify new children to enroll

 Build rapport with parents through home visits and parents meetings

 Following up on irregular children in the class, ensuring high percentage of attendance

in class

 Collect community contributions.

Door Step School

2. Create and maintain an inviting learning environment

 Make optimum use of the classroom space

 Ensure that materials needed for class are requisitioned and received on time

 Ensure class is clean and materials needed for the day are prepared before class

begins

 Record attendance daily and employ methods by which to encourage high levels of

attendance

 Build a rapport with and amongst the children and create an environment where

children are encouraged to learn, share and express themselves

 Use democratic techniques of disciplining

 Write monthly reports that includes statistical data on student attendance and

performance, information on special events, interesting observations of children, case

studies and success stories

3. Create lesson plans that engage students and develop their intellectual and social

skills

 Use a variety of methods to ensure cooperative, effective and active learning that

builds rational, reflective and analytical thinking

 Develop curriculum and activities that:

-Builds vocabulary and develop language skills

-Builds social skills

-Encourages questioning and critical thinking

-Encourages student participation in the class

-Encourages observation of the physical and social environment

-Builds confidence and self esteem of the student

 Prepare tests and question papers to accurately measure student progress

 Conduct parent meetings wherein information on a student’s academic and non-

academic performance is shared

 Conduct ongoing assessments of the students and tailor curriculum to fill gaps when

needed

5. Administrative Responsibilities

 Conduct basic accounting duties for community contributions, petty cash, conveyance

reimbursements

 Keep stock registers

Required Competencies

 Able to use limited resources optimally

 Willing to employ a variety of teaching methods that make learning active, fun and

effective

 Able to accurately gauge areas in which students need improvement and develop

lessons to meet those needs including assigning work appropriately

 Comfortable working with diverse students who often come from difficult backgrounds

 Able to serve as a role model for children in the class

Pay: From ₹8,500.00 per month

Work Location: Remote

How we hire & train our facilitators.

At Sparkling Mindz, we are thoughtful about who we bring into our classrooms because the right adult can make all the difference in a child's journey.

You’ll help children connect, question, and create. This role is for you if: You think marks aren’t enough. You believe every child can think. You want to build the future of school. - WHAT YOU’LL DO 1. Design Learning, Not Lessons - Build child-centric learning outcomes tied to real-world skills, not textbook pages - Create games, materials, and provocations using Reggio-Emilia principles - Co-plan with team to connect Science with Stories, Kannada with Confidence, Social Studies with Systems Thinking 2. Facilitate Thinking, Not Lecturing - Run sessions where children lead discussions, ask “why”, and build answers together - Observe children daily — not just what they write, but how they think - Document learning patterns and share crisp weekly updates with mentors + parents 3. Iterate & Co-Create - Take feedback from children, peers, mentors. Adapt plans fast - Co-teach with other facilitators. Math meets Art. Hindi meets Design Thinking - Design “emergent sessions” based on what children are curious about this week 4. Partner With Parents - Keep parents in the loop on thinking growth, not just test scores - Run 1 parent touchpoint/month — demo class, reflection circle, or portfolio share 5. Grow With Us - Attend weekly team huddles + training. We learn before children do - Bring your ideas — new games, books, tools, ways to make learning stick - 1-year training + probation. We invest heavily in your growth - WHO YOU ARE Must-Haves: 1. Graduate/Post-Graduate from any recognized university 2. Fluent communicator — you listen more than you speak, and speak so children understand 3. Growth mindset — you learn fast, take feedback, and love “what if” questions 4. Tech fluent — MS Office, Google Suite, Canva. You figure tools out 5. Child-first heart — you respect children, enjoy their chaos, and see potential over performance Big Plus If You Have: 1. Experience with children — teaching, camps, volunteering, your own kids 2. Background in Psychology, Education, Counselling, or Creative Arts 3. Skills in storytelling, theatre, public speaking, design, writing, coding 4. Exposure to Reggio-Emilia, IB, Montessori, or other progressive methods Not For You If: You need a textbook to teach. You believe in ranks. You want one-on-one counselling, not group facilitation. Pay: Based on demonstrated skills + market standards. We pay for potential + performance.

salary:
JOB DESCRIPTION- PHYSICAL EDUCATION TEACHER

At Neev, learning is both the guiding principle and the outcome of our purpose, culture, and
environment—creating a lighthouse of learning in India. Teachers plan and design learning
influenced by an understanding of students’ prior knowledge, identities, background, needs and
context. They bridge the learning, by bringing the world into their classroom or taking the
students across to an environment where they experience the learning. Thus, students construct
meaning and make sense of the world through the interplay of asking, doing and thinking,
leading to open, democratic classrooms. Teachers engage in cycles of inquiry, action and
reflection that lead to deeper understanding and lifelong learning. Teachers meet programme
requirements in accordance with the accrediting agencies. They approximately spend 60% to
70% of their time in direct instruction/contact with students and 40% to 30% in preparation,
grading, feedback, meetings, vigilance, and other responsibilities.

Core Responsibilities:

 Plan, organise, and oversee inter-school and intra-school competitions, tournaments,
friendlies, weekend sports programmes, seasonal camps, Annual Sports Day (Sarvajeet
Divas), Neev Aikyam, SrijaNeev, non-curricular days, and other school events in
collaboration with internal and external stakeholders.

 Design, prepare, and deliver Physical Education programmes aligned with school
requirements, including lesson planning, assessment, reporting, student wellbeing,
behaviour management, use of technology, and communication with students, parents,
and colleagues.

 Monitor, assess, and support student participation, performance, and development in
Physical Education, sports, co-curricular activities, competitions, and leadership
opportunities, while providing guidance for professional training and competitive
pathways.

 Manage and supervise before- and after-school sports and activities, Individual and
Collaborative Learning (ICL) clubs, sports facilitators, coaches, external experts, and
other activity providers to ensure high-quality student experiences.

 Liaise with ISSO, TAISI, sports associations, external organisations, and community
partners to facilitate competitions, registrations, partnerships, service-learning
opportunities, CAS initiatives, student leadership programmes, and sports- and
activities-related career exploration.

 Lead the planning, procurement, inventory management, maintenance, and safe use of
sports facilities, equipment, instructional resources, and related budgets to support
curriculum delivery and programme operations.

 Contribute to student support programmes, learning journeys, field trips, study periods,
clubs, school events, professional learning, faculty collaboration, and other
responsibilities assigned by the Reporting Manager while staying current with
developments in sports education and coaching practices.

As A Teacher:

Below are the day-to-day responsibilities :

Section A: Class instructions
 Make learning objectives and expectations clear.
 Explain concepts making them accessible.
 Present well-structured and coherent lessons with a logical sequence of activities and tasks.
 Pace lessons just right, not too fast, and not too slow, finishing on time.
 Use relevant subject vocabulary.
 Build knowledge that is appropriate for the subject / Programme.
 Employ a variety of activities/tools to build engagement and understanding.
 Link topics to prior knowledge.
 Use examples/activities where concepts have real-life contexts.
 Set guided tasks to consolidate learning.

Section B: Assessments and Feedback
 Align assessments with classroom learning.
 Employ purposeful and varied assessment techniques.
 Unpacks assessment criteria for successful task completion.
 Deconstruct examples that help understand requirements for a task.
 Provide clear and actionable feedback (pre/post tests) that furthers understanding.
 Create time for students to reflect on performance feedback and goals.
 Return test and assignment within a reasonable period (4-7 days).
 Be fair and impartial in grading.
 Show an awareness of all students’ capability.
 Prepare students to cope with examinations.

Section C: Classroom environment
 Demonstrate and Instill enthusiasm and passion for the subject.
 Model behaviour and attitudes s/he expects from students.
 Be approachable and responsive to students' needs.
 Use effective questioning techniques to nurture a classroom culture of thinking.
 Set clear instructions and expectations for students with fair and consistent discipline.
 Manage learning spaces, for students to inquire and learn in an optimal and age appropriate
way.
 Engage the majority of students during the lesson.
 Establish peer mentoring or support systems to help students connect with and support each
other.
 Balance student motivation (allowing student voice and choice) without compromising
disciplinary thinking.
 Use technology effectively to enhance learning.
 Conduct one-on-one sessions with students to address personal concerns, academic
challenges, and emotional well-being in times of need.

SECTION D: Course Management
 Prepare unit plans and identify resources (readings, videos and other materials) relevant to
the subject.
 Provide evidence of students' learning that reflects growth in knowledge, conceptual
understandings, skills and dispositions.
 Respond to all communications from parents regarding student learning and wellbeing
within 24hrs.
 Alert the heads if syllabus coverage or assessment tasks have fallen behind.
 Participate in the department/section review cycle to discuss curriculum, student
engagement/behaviour, parent involvement and ongoing schedules.
 Analyze, interpret and report on student assessment data. Also, identify targeted
interventions that improve student learning.
 Participate in professional learning to promote a shared commitment to continuous
improvement.

Please Note:

 Teachers are required to travel for Neev Trust-related activities, including educational
excursions, learning journeys, and field trips. They are also expected to support student
learning through study periods, clubs, and co-curricular programs. Participation in all
school events is mandatory.

 Additional Responsibilities will be given to you based on your strengths.

This Job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities,
duties and responsibilities that are required of the employee for the job. Activities, duties and
responsibilities may change at any time with or without notice. A link to the updated version will
be made available to your team and any changes will reflect the same and imply a change in your
duties. You will be kept informed of the same by your lead. If you are given additional
responsibilities of a temporary nature through mutual discussions with your Leader, then the JD
for the additional role will be made available to you.

The Primary Learning Support Teacher plays a pivotal role in ensuring that children aged 2 to 10 with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND), complex behavioural difficulties, and social-emotional needs can fully access the curriculum.

This role requires a compassionate, highly adaptable educator who is confident working across early childhood and primary stages—with a strong comfort level in early years settings (ages 2–6). The successful candidate will deliver direct academic and behavioural interventions, guide classroom adaptations, and provide structured oversight, coaching, and direction to 1:1 shadow teachers and Teaching Assistants.

*1. Teaching, Remedial & Behavioural Support*

· Plan and deliver individualised and small-group support to address gaps in early literacy, numeracy, communication, and motor skills.

· Design and implement proactive behaviour management strategies, sensory routines, and de-escalation plans tailored to early childhood and primary developmental stages.

· Adapt learning environments and play-based or academic activities to ensure active participation for children, promoting independence and emotional regulation.

· Monitor early developmental milestones and provide timely, targeted remedial interventions.

*2. Leadership & Support for 1:1 Shadow Teachers*

· Provide daily guidance, mentoring, and line-management support to 1:1 shadow teachers and learning support assistants.

· Collaborate with 1:1 shadow teachers to establish clear daily goals, consistent behaviour strategies, and effective scaffolding techniques for their assigned students.

· Conduct regular check-ins with shadow teachers to review student progress, adapt strategies, and foster professional growth within the support team.

*3. Collaboration & Curriculum Access*

· Partner with early years practitioners, primary class teachers, and subject specialists to adapt curricula, learning materials, and assessment methods.

· Model inclusive classroom strategies and positive behaviour management techniques for teaching staff.

· Contribute to school-wide staff development regarding early inclusion practices and neurodiversity awareness.

*4. Assessment, Tracking & Compliance*

· Conduct observational assessments, diagnostic tracking, and developmental evaluations to measure progress against Pupil Passports & Individual Education Plans (IEPs) and behavioural targets.

· Maintain accurate, confidential, and comprehensive student records in compliance with school policies and statutory safeguarding standards.

· Continuously evaluate intervention effectiveness to refine support plans and lead smooth transitions across primary year groups.

*5. Family & External Stakeholder Engagement*

· Build warm, authentic relationships with parents and carers, maintaining open communication about developmental progress, behavioural milestones, and home strategies.

· Lead parent meetings, workshops, and case conferences with empathy and clarity.

· Collaborate with speech and language therapists, occupational therapists, educational psychologists, and medical professionals to maintain unified care plans.

*6. Operational & Co-Curricular Duties*

· Assist with supervision and medication administration according to school policies and medical protocols.

· Contribute actively to the House system, Co-Curricular Activities (CCA) programme, and early childhood events.

· *Education*: Bachelor’s degree / Diploma in Education, Early Childhood Education, Special Needs Education, or an equivalent discipline.

Pay: ₹40,000.00 - ₹65,000.00 per month

Job Designation: Dean – Sarla Anil Surendra Modi School of Economics

Job Summary: To provide strategic academic and administrative leadership to the Sarla Anil Surendra Modi School of Economics (SAMSOE), ensuring academic excellence, high-quality teaching and research, curriculum development, faculty growth, student success, and institutional development. The Dean will lead the School’s academic and administrative activities, strengthen industry and academic partnerships, promote innovation, and align the School’s objectives with the vision and policies of NMIMS.

Designation

Dean – Sarla Anil Surendra Modi School of Economics

Location

Mumbai

Department

Dean's Office

Key Responsibilities

Establish and implement academic and administrative policies approved by NMIMS.

Lead academic planning, curriculum development, and quality enhancement.

Oversee faculty recruitment, development, and academic performance.

Promote research, publications, and interdisciplinary academic initiatives.

Oversee admissions, student development, academic progress, and placements.

Plan and coordinate academic events, seminars, conferences, and School activities.

Develop industry partnerships and academic collaborations nationally and internationally.

Ensure accreditation, regulatory compliance, and academic quality assurance.

Oversee budgeting, resource allocation, and effective utilisation of School resources.

Promote innovative teaching methods and initiatives aligned with NMIMS’s vision and the School’s strategic objectives.

Educational Qualification

Ph.D. in Economics or an allied/relevant discipline from a recognised University/Institution.

Qualifications shall be as per applicable UGC Regulations and the University’s approved Recruitment Rules.

The candidate should be at Professor level in a premier management school or be a Principal of a premier undergraduate college.

Professional Experience

Minimum 15 years of academic and administrative experience in higher education, preferably in Economics or a related discipline.

 A demonstrated record of high-quality research, publications, academic leadership, and institutional development.

Experience in academic administration, programme development, accreditation, quality assurance, and industry or institutional collaboration.

Skills and Competencies

Strong academic leadership, strategic planning, and decision-making skills.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, and team-management abilities.
Expertise in curriculum development, academic innovation, and research.
Sound administrative, financial, and resource-management capabilities.
Knowledge of accreditation, regulatory compliance, and academic quality assurance.
Student-centric approach with strong industry and academic relationship-building skills.
In 1981, Shri Vile Parle Kelavani Mandal (SVKM) established Narsee Monjee Institute of Management Studies (NMIMS) to meet the growing demand for management education. In 2003, NMIMS was declared a deemed to be university under Section 3 of the UGC Act 1956. The Vision of the University is to be a globally admired University by 2030. The Mission of NMIMS is to emerge as a Centre of Excellence, best in class in India and Asia and yearning to be the best in the world by 2030.

With the legacy of 40 years, NMIMS has grown to being not only one of the top-10 B-schools in India but also emerged as a multi-disciplinary, multi-campus University at Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Indore, Shirpur, Dhule, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Chandigarh and seventeen constituent schools that include Management, Family Business, Engineering, Pharmacy, Architecture, Commerce, Economics, Law, Science, Liberal Arts, Design, Performing Arts, Mathematical Science, Agricultural Science, Hospitality Management, Branding & Advertising and Distance Learning. In addition, we have nine Centres of Excellence as well at the University.

The consistent academic quality, research focus, faculty from top national and global institutes and strong industry linkages at NMIMS have placed it amongst the nation's prime centres of educational excellence and research today. More than 17000 students and about 750 full-time faculty members, 10 faculty members with Fulbright Scholarship and Humboldt International Scholarship for post-doctoral researchers are part of India's most sought after academic community.

*## Job Summary*

We are seeking a dynamic and empathetic Admission Counsellor to join our team. The ideal candidate should possess excellent communication and interpersonal skills, a background in counselling or education, and aprior experience in student recruitment, admissions, or educational counselling will be preferred. The Admission Counsellor will serve as the first point of contact for prospective families, playing a crucial role in guiding them through the admission process, showcasing the school’s values, and ensuring a positive and welcoming experience that converts inquiries into enrolled students.

*## Responsibilities*

Ø Serve as the primary point of contact for all prospective parents and students, responding to phone calls, emails, and in-person inquiries promptly and professionally.

Ø Conduct informative and engaging campus tours and presentations for prospective families, effectively communicating the school's vision, mission, curriculum, facilities, and unique selling points (USPs).

Ø Coordinate and oversee the admission assessments or student interactions, ensuring a smooth and stress-free experience for the child.

Ø Maintain accurate records of all inquiries, applications, and enrollment data in the school's management system.

Ø Liaise with the academic coordinators, principal, and accounts department to ensure a seamless transition from admission to onboarding for new students.

Ø Clearly communicate school policies, fee structures, and rules and regulations to parents, ensuring transparency and managing expectations.

Ø Assist in planning and executing admission-related events to maximize outreach and enrollment.

Ø Stay updated on current educational trends, competitor schools, and market demands to provide feedback to the management for marketing and outreach strategies.

Ø Foster long-term relationships with parents even after admission to ensure a high level of satisfaction and encourage word-of-mouth referrals.

*## Skills*

Ø Expertise in customer relationship management with the ability to build immediate rapport and trust with diverse families.

Ø Ability to guide and influence decision-making while maintaining a high level of empathy and ethical conduct.

Ø An engaging and confident presentation style, capable of commanding attention during public speaking and campus tours.

Ø Intelligent and thoughtful communicator, both orally and in writing, with a flair for sales and persuasion.

Ø Strong organizational skills with high attention to detail to manage multiple applications and follow-ups simultaneously.

Ø Flexible and adaptable, responding positively to the dynamic nature of the admission season and changing targets.

Ø Proficient in handling IT platforms and strong technical skills.

Ø Social, result-oriented mentor and leader focused on achieving enrolment goals and committed to delivering a high-quality parent experience.

Ø Strong communication, interpersonal, and presentation skills.

Graduate/P postgraduate in any stream

Experience as an Admission Counsellor or similar role in a CBSE school is preferred

Graduate/P postgraduate in any stream (A degree in Psychology, Counselling, or Mass Communication is an added advantage).
